subject: Immediate action requested: dedicated pool surge impacting ShoreBank reserved throughput (retention risk)
messages:
From: Liz Matthews <liz.matthews@shorebank.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@shorebank.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in errors & latency — ShoreBank reserved throughput impacted

Marissa —

We're seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors and tail-latency from your dedicated GPU pool that backs our production inference (env: payments-prod) starting around 01:30 UTC this morning. Error rate rose to ~7% and p95 latency jumped from ~160ms to ~1.2s for several windows. This is causing timeouts in our downstream payment gateway and two outages in the last 3 hours.

We have an upcoming retention review with the CTO next week; if this continues we will need to consider alternate inference routing and pause expansion. We need an immediate stabilization plan and confirmation on whether you can provide temporary burst capacity or a short-term SLA credit while you investigate.

Attached is a short log extract and the transaction IDs for the incidents.

Thanks,
Liz
Director, Engineering — ShoreBank
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Liz Matthews <liz.matthews@shorebank.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in errors & latency — ShoreBank reserved throughput impacted

Liz — thank you for the alert and the incident details. I’m sorry for the disruption. We take this very seriously.

Immediate actions we’ve kicked off (ops already on it):
- Fixed-rate routing for ShoreBank model traffic to an isolation slice to limit noisy-neighbor bleed.
- Short-term KV cache warmup and prefix caching enabled for your hot endpoints.
- Rolling restart of the dedicated pool allocation for your reservation to clear a suspected kernel-level degradation.

Neha (ops lead) is on a bridge now and will provide metrics in ~20 minutes. Vivek, I’m looping you in because the customer mentioned retention review and requested credits — need exec visibility for any non-standard concessions.

Can you confirm the time window for the ongoing errors (if they persist) and whether you can route non-urgent traffic to the canary endpoint (we can provide a temporary host/port)? Also attaching the SLA usage report for context.

I’ll follow with a short mitigation note once ops confirms stabilization.

— Marissa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Liz Matthews <liz.matthews@shorebank.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in errors & latency — ops update and MAP

Quick ops update (bridge notes):
- Root cause hypothesis: sudden kernel scheduling regression on the NVIDIA stacks for the dedicated pool causing intermittent OOM backoffs under medium sequence lengths. Working with runtime team to test a micro-patch; results expected in 45–60 minutes.
- Mitigations active: traffic isolation, cache warmup, prioritized KV cache allocation. Error rate has fallen from 7% to ~1.6% in the last 12 min but p95 still elevated (~520ms).

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) Immediate: keep isolation slice + enable traffic shaping to limit bursty tails — target bring p95 < 250ms within 3 hours.
2) 0–24h: deploy micro-patch to affected kernel path, monitor.
3) 24–72h: full test rollout with rollback policy.
4) Commercial: provide a one-time usage credit for the impacted window and offer 48h of free burst capacity while we stabilize — requires sales/procurement approval.

Attachments: SLA-usage-report-2028-07-24.csv (shows token volumes by minute).

Neha
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, Liz Matthews <liz.matthews@shorebank.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in errors & latency — approvals and next steps

Team — thanks for the quick response and to ShoreBank for flagging. I’ve reviewed the ops summary and the usage report. Approvals:
- Authorize up to 48 hours of burst capacity for ShoreBank (non-billable) to remove immediate production pressure.
- Approve a discretionary usage credit up to $18,000 for the impacted window pending final postmortem.

Marissa / David — please coordinate an amendment (48h burst + credit) and route it through procurement. David, liaise with Liz on DocuSign and confirm the retention ask so we can prioritize a tailored SLA/counteroffer.

Neha — keep me posted on patch rollout progress; escalate immediately if p95 does not trend down within the promised window.

Vivek
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference
From: Liz Matthews <liz.matthews@shorebank.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@shorebank.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in errors & latency — shorebank confirmation and DocuSign

Marissa / David — thanks for the support and the burst allocation; systems returned to normal after the micro-patch and the isolation changes. p95 is back to ~170–200ms and error rate stable <0.5%.

We’re prepared to accept the 48h burst and the proposed credit, but need the amendment and a short note committing to a postmortem and timeline for a permanent fix before our CTO retention meeting on Aug 2. Ravi and I will sign the DocuSign when available.

Please send the amendment and the postmortem plan link.

Regards,
Liz
Director, Engineering — ShoreBank
